classification.difficultyReason: Identify unbroken graphs, a vertical asymptote, a hole and a jump, then read the discontinuity coordinates; recognise that a joined corner is continuous.

content.prompt: Categorise the following as either continuous or discontinuous functions over the domain $x\in\mathbb{R}$. For the functions that are discontinuous in that domain, state the value(s) of $x$ where the discontinuity has occurred.

spec.description: Increasing straight line crosses the y-axis above the origin and the x-axis to its left. Arrows at both line ends; no numerical ticks.
spec.mathematics: Unbroken linear graph; unlabelled coordinates are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Given graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: The straight-line graph has no breaks for any real $x$.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola symmetric about the y-axis, vertex below the x-axis, arrows at both upper ends and no numerical ticks.
spec.mathematics: Unbroken parabolic graph; unlabelled coordinates are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Given graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: The parabola has no breaks for any real $x$.

spec.description: Reciprocal-shaped branches about the dashed vertical asymptote labelled x=1, close to the right of the y-axis. Horizontal asymptote is the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Vertical asymptote x=1; the horizontal drawing scale is schematic and the sole numerical x label identifies the asymptote.
spec.answerVisibility: Given graph and asymptote label visible in all editions.

answer.worked: The graph approaches a vertical asymptote at $x=1$, so it has an asymptotic discontinuity there.

spec.description: Increasing line with an open circle above x=1, dashed vertical guide and x-axis tick labelled 1.
spec.mathematics: A hole at x=1; unlabelled vertical scale is schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Given graph and hole visible in all editions.

answer.worked: The open circle shows a hole at $x=1$, so the function is discontinuous there.

spec.description: Upper rightward ray at π/2 and lower leftward ray at −π/2, both with open endpoints on the y-axis. Upper label left and lower label right of the axis.
spec.mathematics: Unequal one-sided values π/2 and −π/2 at x=0.
spec.answerVisibility: Given graph, open endpoints and values visible in all editions.

answer.worked: The graph jumps from $-\frac{\pi}{2}$ to $\frac{\pi}{2}$ at $x=0$, and both endpoints there are open.

spec.description: Two upward rays meet at the origin to form a V. No gap or open circle at the vertex.
spec.mathematics: Continuous V-shaped graph, including at its corner.
spec.answerVisibility: Given graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: The two rays meet without a gap at the origin. A corner does not break continuity.
